issues.legal_issue: Whether payment made to obtain a lease is capital or revenue expenditure depends on the lease’s object and the nature of the payment, not merely on whether the lease conveys an interest in land.
material_facts: The lease was for a short period and the finding that it covered removal of sand lying loose on the surface, without excavation or skillful extraction, was affirmed by the Tribunal.
The sand was the assessee’s stock-in-trade, and the lease payment enabled the assessee to obtain it for the business.
The lease granted rights to enter and occupy the land, but the expenditure was not for acquiring an enduring asset or reserving a source to be excavated or worked.
issues.conclusion: The lease payments were revenue expenditure deductible in computing income; the fact that the lease conveyed an interest in land did not make them capital expenditure.
issues.legal_principle: The character of expenditure must be determined from the facts of each case, including the object of the lease and the nature of the payment. Under the approach in Gotan Lime Syndicate v. Commissioner of Income-tax and Bombay Steam Navigation Co. (1953) (P.) Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax, expenditure integral to the business’s profit-earning process and not incurred to acquire an asset or permanent right may be revenue expenditure. K.T.M.T.M. Abul Kayoom v. Commissioner of Income-tax was distinguished because it concerned payment to reserve an exclusive source that had to be worked in the sea.

rule.if: income_tax_deduction_case and short_term_lease and surface_material_removal and material_is_stock_in_trade and no_excavation_or_skillful_extraction and no_enduring_asset_acquired

predicates.income_tax_deduction_case: The proceeding concerns whether a business expense is deductible in an income-tax assessment.
predicates.short_term_lease: The business obtained the relevant right under a lease of short duration.
predicates.surface_material_removal: The lease enabled removal of material lying loose on the surface.
predicates.material_is_stock_in_trade: The material obtained through the lease was stock-in-trade of the business.
predicates.no_excavation_or_skillful_extraction: Obtaining the material did not require excavation or skillful extraction.
predicates.no_enduring_asset_acquired: The expenditure did not acquire an asset or right of an enduring or permanent character.

issues.definition: When a business expense in an income-tax deduction case is paid under a short-term lease to obtain surface material that is its stock-in-trade, without excavation or acquisition of an enduring asset, the payment is revenue expenditure deductible.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court deciding a tax reference must accept an affirmed factual finding when no question has been referred challenging that finding as unsupported by evidence.
material_facts: The Appellate Assistant Commissioner found that the sand lay loose on the surface and that the contract required only its removal, without excavation or skillful extraction.
The Tribunal affirmed that finding and recorded that it had not been challenged before it.
No question was referred to the High Court alleging that the finding lacked evidentiary support, but the High Court reached a different factual conclusion.
issues.conclusion: The High Court exceeded its jurisdiction by rejecting the affirmed factual finding and substituting a different finding.
issues.legal_principle: In a tax reference, a factual finding affirmed by the Tribunal is binding on the High Court unless a question challenging it as based on no evidence is referred; the High Court must decide the legal issue on the basis of that finding.

predicates.income_tax_reference_case: The proceeding asks a High Court to answer a legal question referred from a tax tribunal.
predicates.tribunal_affirmed_factual_finding: The tribunal affirmed a factual finding made by the lower appellate authority.
predicates.no_referred_challenge_to_evidentiary_bas: No referred question asks whether the factual finding was unsupported by evidence.

issues.definition: In an income-tax reference, when the tribunal has affirmed a factual finding and no referred question challenges its evidentiary basis, the High Court must accept that finding.
